domains.name: Server Shop & Player Market
domains.promise: Members spend and earn play-money coins across two owner-controlled trading surfaces: an owner-curated server shop (/shop, /buy, /sell) whose items, prices, and stock the owner defines, and an opt-in player-to-player market (/market list, browse, buy, my-listings, cancel) where members trade their own items under an atomic no-double-sell purchase RPC and a configurable market fee sink. Every coin and item here is fake game economy — and the anti-laundering wall is absolute: items granted by a real-money commerce purchase are never listable or sellable on the player market, and commerce-held roles earn no game income.

controls.description: Master economy switch (economy_enabled) that gates the server shop; when off, /shop, /buy, and /sell explain the economy is disabled.
Player-to-player market switch (economy_market_enabled); when off, /market subcommands reply that the market is disabled while the server shop keeps working.
Percentage market fee (economy_market_fee_pct) skimmed from each player-market sale as a play-money coin sink; the seller receives the remainder.
How many days (economy_market_listing_days) a player-market listing stays active before it expires and stops accepting buys.
Maximum simultaneously active listings (economy_market_max_listings) one member may hold on the player market.
Hard ceiling on a listing's price per unit (the MAX_PRICE_PER_UNIT guard) that rejects absurd listings well below the safe-integer limit.

The anti-laundering wall: when on, any item whose origin is a real-money commerce purchase (a non-tradeable item) is permanently barred from the player market; this guardrail is locked on and cannot be disabled by the owner.

defaults.rationale: The server shop is the core coin sink of the game economy and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience.
Player-to-player trading is a coin-movement surface, so it ships off as a deliberate guardrail until the owner opts in and sets a fee.
A light 5 percent sink keeps the market liquid while gently draining coins out of circulation.
A one-week listing window balances discoverability against stale listings clogging the board.
Ten active listings per member is generous for casual sellers while preventing one member from flooding the market.
A one-billion-coin ceiling sits far above any realistic wallet yet safely inside the JS safe-integer range, blocking absurd or overflow listings.
Real-money items must never become a laundering path into the play-money market; the wall is locked on by design and cannot be turned off.

permissions.action: Run /shop, /buy, and /sell against the owner-curated server shop
permissions.enforcement: Shop slash commands respond for every member; /buy and /sell only ever debit or credit the invoking member's own wallet and inventory rows.

permissions.action: Run /market list, browse, buy, my-listings, and cancel on the player market
permissions.enforcement: Market commands respond for every member; list, buy, and cancel handlers key every mutation to the invoking member's own id and the listing's guild id.

permissions.actor: Dashboard user with owner or admin access to the guild
permissions.action: Create and edit shop items and market settings on the dashboard economy pages
permissions.enforcement: Dashboard session auth plus Supabase RLS restrict economy_items and guild_config writes to authorized guild administrators.

permissions.action: List or sell an item granted by a real-money commerce purchase on the player market
permissions.enforcement: The listing path must reject any non-tradeable, commerce-origin item before any inventory decrement so a real-money grant can never be converted into market income.

permissions.action: Cancel or force-settle another member's active market listing
permissions.enforcement: The atomic cancel RPC is keyed to the invoking member's seller id; no code path cancels or mutates another member's listing row.

messages.trigger: A member buys an item from the server shop with play-money coins
messages.audience: The buying member and the channel

messages.trigger: A member lists one of their own items on the player market
messages.audience: The listing member and the channel
messages.defaultTemplate: Listed {quantity}x {item-name} at {price-per-unit} coins each on the player market.

messages.trigger: A member buys from an active player-market listing
messages.audience: The buying member and the channel
messages.defaultTemplate: Purchase complete: {quantity}x {item-name} for {total-cost} coins after a {fee}-coin market fee.

messages.trigger: A member tries to list a commerce-granted, non-tradeable item on the player market
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the invoking member
messages.defaultTemplate: {item-name} was granted through a real-money purchase and can never be listed on the player market.

messages.trigger: A market purchase debited the buyer but a downstream payout or delivery step failed
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the invoking member
messages.defaultTemplate: That purchase did not go through, {member-name} — your coins are already back in your wallet and nothing was lost.

messages.trigger: The shop or market backend is temporarily unreachable when a member runs a command
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the invoking member
messages.defaultTemplate: The market stall is catching its breath, {member-name} — give it a moment and try again.

messages.trigger: A cancelled listing's item return to inventory keeps failing
messages.defaultTemplate: Heads up: returning {quantity}x {item-name} from a cancelled listing failed and is queued for automatic retry; nothing was duplicated and everything is logged.

values.description: The player market is off by configuration; /market replies market-disabled while the server shop, /buy, and /sell keep working.
The player market is enabled; members can list, browse, buy, and cancel listings under the configured fee and caps.
A member's listing is live with remaining above zero; the listed items are escrowed out of the seller's inventory.
Atomic buys drove a listing's remaining to zero; it is marked sold and accepts no further purchases.
The seller cancelled the listing and the escrowed items were returned to their inventory.
A cancel flipped the listing to cancelled but the inventory return failed; the return is queued for automatic reconciliation with nothing lost or duplicated.

transitions.trigger: Owner turns economy_market_enabled on from the dashboard
transitions.expectedEffect: The player market opens live without a restart; /market list, browse, and buy begin responding under the configured fee and caps.

transitions.trigger: A member runs /market list with a tradeable item they own
transitions.expectedEffect: economy_market_atomic_create_listing decrements the seller's stack and inserts the listing in one locked transaction, escrowing the exact quantity with no oversell.

transitions.trigger: Buyers purchase the last remaining units via /market buy
transitions.expectedEffect: economy_market_buy atomically decrements remaining to zero, the buyer is debited once, and the seller is credited the total minus the market fee.

transitions.trigger: The seller runs /market cancel on their own active listing
transitions.expectedEffect: economy_market_atomic_cancel flips status to cancelled only if still active and the escrowed remaining is returned to the seller's inventory exactly once.

transitions.trigger: The listing cancels but the inventory return upsert fails
transitions.expectedEffect: A market_item_reconcile row is queued in bot_action_queue so the item return retries automatically; the member is told nothing was lost.

transitions.trigger: The queued market_item_reconcile action succeeds on retry
transitions.expectedEffect: The escrowed items are returned to the seller's inventory exactly once and the reconciliation entry is marked done.

transitions.trigger: Owner turns economy_market_enabled off from the dashboard
transitions.expectedEffect: /market subcommands reply market-disabled; existing listing rows and escrowed items are preserved untouched.

failures.trigger: economy_add_balance for the seller fails after the buyer was debited and the listing remaining was decremented
failures.expectedBehavior: The buyer is refunded exactly once through economy_add_balance and the listing remaining is restored via economy_market_buy_revert, so no coins are lost, the seller is never paid twice, and the listing returns to purchasable.

failures.trigger: economy_upsert_inventory for the buyer fails after the buyer was debited and the seller was paid
failures.expectedBehavior: The whole purchase unwinds exactly once — the buyer is refunded, the seller credit is clawed back, and the listing remaining is restored — leaving balances and stock byte-identical to before the attempt.

failures.trigger: economy_upsert_inventory fails when returning items from a cancelled listing
failures.expectedBehavior: The cancel stands, a market_item_reconcile job is queued in bot_action_queue for automatic retry, and the items are returned exactly once when it runs — never zero-returned-but-cancelled and never double-returned.

failures.trigger: A member attempts /market list on a commerce-granted, non-tradeable item
failures.expectedBehavior: The listing path rejects the item before any inventory decrement, no listing row is created, the item stays in the member's inventory, and the branded rejection explains real-money items can never be listed.

failures.trigger: Supabase is unreachable when a member runs a shop or market command
failures.expectedBehavior: Commands reply with the branded market-unavailable message and no coins or items move; the outage raises a single degradation alert rather than one per failed command, and a later retry succeeds cleanly.

evidence.expectedObservation: Every shop and market state change in this domain lands exactly one append-only audit row with actor, guild, and correlation id; anonymization, never deletion, is the only mutation observed.

evidence.observer: Owner alert channel observer in the primary test guild
evidence.expectedObservation: This domain's failure branches raise exactly one owner alert carrying a human-readable reason and remediation hint; happy paths raise none.

evidence.observer: Embed and message snapshot inspector comparing captures against the configured brand kit
evidence.expectedObservation: Captured shop and market embeds and messages match the owner's white-label brand kit and configured voice preset, including the subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution.

evidence.expectedObservation: Replaying recorded triggers for this domain against the live stack leaves end state unchanged: no duplicate play-money debits, seller payouts, item deliveries, or listing mutations.
